To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

administration of organic acids in the drinking water of broilers undergoing preslaughter feed withdrawal can reduce the incidence of Salmonella and/or Campylobacter in the crop, and can reduce the incidence and/or number of Salmonella and or Campylobacter recovered from broiler carcass wash samples at the processing plant.

lactic acid treatment of the drinking water during a 10 h preslaughter feed withdrawal reduced the incidence of Salmonella contamination of the crop and the incidence of Salmonellainfection on pre-chill broiler carcasses.
the addition of lactic acid to drinking water during feed withdrawal reduces Salmonella and Camplylobacter contamination of pre-chill carcasses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of organic acids in the drinking water to reduce Salmonella and/or Campylobacter in broiler crops.
the development of a practical method for reducing Salmonella contamination of broiler crops and carcasses at the time of processing.
developing strategies to reduce the incidence of Camplylobacter in broiler flocks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of latic acid in the drinking waters during the feed withdrawal process can reduce the incidence and numbers of Salmonella and Camylobacter in broilers and on broiler carcasses during processing.
the use of 0.44 to 0.50% lactic acid in broiler drinking water during preslaughte
lactic acid in drinking water during pre-slaughter feed withdrawal can reduce the incidence and number of Salmonella and C. jejuni recovered in crop and on broiler carcasses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the administration of lactic acid during the pretransport FW period can reduce the incidence of Camplyobacter and Salmonella in the crop, and in the pre-chill carcasses, but not to the level of the control group.
lactic acid in drinking water during FW reduces Salmonella and Campylbacter contamination in crops, prechill carcasses, and postchill carcass rinse water.
the use of l-lactic acid in the water during the last 4 h of feed withdrawal and during transport reduces the incidence of Salmonella and C. jejuni in broiler carcass rinses at processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can reduce the amount of Campylobacters and Salmonellas in the crop and the carcass by using lactic acid.
lactic acid administration during preslaughter FW may reduce the risk of carcass contamination with Salmonella and Camplylobacter.
the administration of lactic acid during feed withdrawal can reduce Salmonella and/or Campylobacter on the crop and on broiler carcasses.
